methodology: Both the original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements that each represent a distinct aspect of the clock's functionality or design.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Design a 12-hour clock with AM/PM indication.
Use BCD counters for hours, minutes, and seconds.
Clock is driven by a fast clock signal 'clk'.
Hours range from 01 to 12 in BCD.
Minutes range from 00 to 59 in BCD.
Seconds range from 00 to 59 in BCD.
Synchronous active-high reset signal resets the clock to 12:00 AM.
'pm' signal toggles when the hour counter transitions from 11 to 12.
spec_atomic_units: Module has inputs clk, reset, and ena.
Module has output pm.
Module has outputs hh, mm, and ss as 8-bit registers.
clk is a fast-running clock signal.
reset is an active-high synchronous reset signal.
reset forces the clock to 12:00 AM.
reset has the highest priority.
ena enables the clock to increment.
When ena is low, the clock holds its current value.
pm indicates AM (0) or PM (1).
hh represents hours in BCD format (01-12).
mm represents minutes in BCD format (00-59).
ss represents seconds in BCD format (00-59).
Seconds increment logic increments ss from 00 to 59.
Seconds increment logic resets ss to 00 when it reaches 59 and asserts a carry-out.
Minutes increment logic increments mm when seconds carry-out is asserted.
Minutes increment logic resets mm to 00 when it reaches 59 and asserts a carry-out.
Hours increment logic increments hh when minutes carry-out is asserted.
Hours increment logic resets hh to 01 when it reaches 12.
AM/PM logic toggles pm when hh transitions from 11 to 12.
AM/PM logic sets pm to 0 (AM) on reset.
BCD conversion logic ensures values remain in BCD format.
Reset logic sets hh to 12, mm to 00, ss to 00, and pm to 0 on reset.
The clock operates synchronously with the rising edge of the `clk` signal.
The `reset` signal, when asserted high, synchronously resets the clock to 12:00 AM on the next rising edge of `clk`.
The `ena` signal, when asserted high, enables the incrementing of the seconds counter on the next rising edge of `clk`.
The `pm` signal toggles when the hour counter transitions from 11 to 12, also synchronized to the rising edge of `clk`.
The outputs `hh`, `mm`, and `ss` update their values on the rising edge of `clk` when the respective counters are incremented.
The critical paths include the reset path from the `reset` input to the registers for `hh`, `mm`, `ss`, and `pm`.
The setup time for the `reset` signal must be met with respect to the rising edge of `clk` to ensure proper reset operation.
The setup time for the `ena` signal must be met with respect to the rising edge of `clk` to ensure proper incrementing of the counters.
The propagation delay through the combinational logic for incrementing the counters and updating the `pm` signal must be less than the clock period to ensure correct operation.
The circuit is a sequential circuit with synchronous behavior triggered by the rising edge of the `clk` signal.
It contains at least four registers: `pm`, `hh`, `mm`, and `ss`.
The registers are updated using non-blocking assignments (`<=`) within an `always @(posedge clk)` block.
The `reset` signal has priority, so if `reset` is high, all registers are set to their initial values (12:00 AM).
Otherwise, if `ena` is high, the seconds counter is incremented.
When the seconds counter reaches 60, it resets to 0, and the minutes counter is incremented.
Similarly, when the minutes counter reaches 60, it resets to 0, and the hours counter is incremented.
When the hours counter transitions from 11 to 12, the `pm` signal is toggled.
The `hh`, `mm`, and `ss` registers are declared as `reg [7:0]`, and the `pm` register is declared as `reg`.
